search.description: This part encodes BoPep4, a 23-residue plant elicitor peptide (PEP) from broccoli (*Brassica oleracea var. italica);* the wild-type BoPep4 sequence is registered as [BBa\_26ILD3SO](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ild3so)*.* BoPep4 acts as a peptide hormone and signaling molecule to regulate plant defense mechanisms and salt tolerance. In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site.

documentation.title: Application
documentation.value:
This part was designed for the GEMS-Taiwan 2026 iGEM team’s work on a Stress-Responsive Optogenetic Bioreactor for Precision Plant Protection and is used in the construction of composite parts:

* **SamyQ-BoPep4 2.2-Histag** ([<u>BBa\_267B69E3</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-267b69e3) ): The BoPep4 protein, a C-terminally encoded plant elicitor peptide derived from broccoli, is fused to the SamyQ signal peptide at the N-terminus and a 6x Histag at the C-terminus.
* **Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ-BoPep4 2.2-Histag-B0015** ([<u>BBa\_26IA55UY</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ia55uy) ): this Protectant Module constitutively expresses potential stress-mitigation proteins and enables evaluation of their secretion and detection, with its constitutive promoter Pveg, RBS EEBD-RBS0, and terminator B0015.

documentation.title: Design
documentation.value:
## **About**

* **Biosafety level:** S1 
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* \[168 / WB800] 
* In this variant, the first 15 codons of the BoPep4 coding sequence were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site.

## Dry lab / computational analysis

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/db789e4a-bc1e-43a6-8afd-de6ca8e4cbc4/b8766a706c1563004798167ebc968c6c37fb1bdc8ab7e6f71e9a6c0a198a09bd.avif)

**Figure 1. BoPep4 bound to the plant receptor PEPR1.** (a) The PEPR1 ectodomain, residues 29-738 (710 modelled), shown as a grey surface, with BoPep4 — BoPep4 1-23, Gly1 to Asn23 — in orange, lying in the inner groove of the leucine-rich-repeat solenoid. This is the starting structure of every molecular dynamics run in this document, threaded onto the 5GR8 (PEPR1-AtPep1) crystal structure of PEPR1 with AtPep1. Teal patches are the eight crystallographic contact residues: Asp273, Val297, Asp348, Phe371, Asp441, Ile443, Asn465, Arg487. (b) The Asn23 clamp, the interaction the peptide works through. The free C-terminal carboxylate of Asn23 is gripped by the Arg487 guanidinium (orange dashes); Asn465 and Asp441 complete the clamp. This is the contact that the molecular dynamics tracks, and the one a C-terminal purification tag destroys. BoPep4 is a 23-amino-acid plant elicitor peptide from broccoli. Binding PEPR1 switches on the plant's own salt-tolerance response, so a small amount of secreted peptide produces a plant-side effect. The pose is a model, not an experimental structure of BoPep4 with PEPR1.



![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/4747c22b-8803-4cb2-867b-03c868f11984/3cafffeb48fc207593b756c73d55241d23d397658833b1237a1cebe136a06304.avif)

**Figure 1. Translation-initiation structure of the BoPep4 v2 top1 cassette.** (a) The ordered design against the wild type, a naive low-GC recoding rule, and the best candidates of a replicate 50,000-variant search; it ranks 4 of 42,581, the top 0.009 % of the pool. (b) Predicted minimum-free-energy secondary structure of the wild-type messenger RNA window — 236 nt: recombination site, MF001 ribosome binding site, SamyQ signal peptide and the first 90 nt of the coding sequence — at -43.2 kcal/mol. (c) The same for the ordered design at -49.1 kcal/mol; the 11 bases that differ from wild type are orange. (d) Probability that each base is unpaired, wild type in grey against the ordered design in green, with the ribosome binding site, the start+15 window and the recoded region shaded. Start-codon accessibility 0.396 → 0.497; ribosome-binding-site accessibility 0.067 → 0.634. All 9 codon changes are synonymous — the protein (GILIGSKKRPREPHS…) and the SamyQ cleavage site are unchanged. ViennaRNA 2.7.2, 37 °C, partition function, noLonelyPairs on.

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/4747c22b-8803-4cb2-867b-03c868f11984/563e8334c64de404d03051fc72350f7d736a8ec67e7d0a851817cfa94bbdebf6.avif)

**Figure 2. Trajectory behaviour of the BoPep4–PEPR1 panel.** Eight peptide-bound systems and the receptor alone, 30 ns each, 1,500 frames; traces are smoothed with a 500 ps rolling average for legibility. (a) Receptor backbone movement against the starting structure. (b) Peptide movement measured in the receptor's frame, so the trace reports displacement within the binding groove rather than the peptide's own flexibility. (c) Shortest distance across the Asn23–Arg487 salt bridge; the grey dashed line is the 2.4 Å separation in the 5GR8 crystal structure. (d) Clamp integrity, the number of four defining contacts made per frame. The ordered 9–23 construct (orange) is the only system at pH 7 whose clamp repeatedly opens and closes, and at pH 5.5 (purple) it leaves the 4 Å shell within 2 ns and does not return. OpenMM 8, AMBER ff19SB, OPC water, 0.15 M NaCl, full 710-residue PEPR1 ectodomain, \~127,000 atoms.

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/4747c22b-8803-4cb2-867b-03c868f11984/5e77975cbd4517b5913e7d0a6fdd871d2b6561102cbc98d68c9dacfc97384706.avif)

**Figure 3. Contact occupancies against the pre-registered acceptance criteria.** Fraction of the 1,500 production frames in which each contact is made: the Arg487 and Asn465 pairs within 4 Å, and the Asn23 clamp at full (4 of 4) and relaxed (at least 3 of 4) stringency. Dashed red lines mark the 60 % pass mark, written down before the runs. BoPep4 9–23 at pH 5.5 is the only system that fails a criterion (23.6 %). At pH 7 the ordered 9–23 construct is the weakest of the panel (Arg487 81.1 %, Asn465 53.3 %, clamp 77.1 %), while the fragment intended as a negative control, 15–23, is indistinguishable from wild type (99.9 %, 97.1 %, 99.9 %).

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/4747c22b-8803-4cb2-867b-03c868f11984/3da62e90de50dc272c219920ddfe0e80e383698564355c9b36b72085a43adc2a.avif)

**Figure 4. The Asn23–Arg487 salt bridge resolved to oxygens and hydrogen bonds.** (a) How the Arg487 guanidinium engages the Asn23 C-terminus: with both terminal oxygens (bidentate), one (monodentate), or neither. (b) What occupies the guanidinium's first shell, split by chemical identity. (c) Distance between the two charge centres, mean ± SD over 1,500 frames. A C-terminal 6×His tag removes the free carboxylate entirely: bidentate engagement falls from 100.0 % to 0.0 % of frames, the peptide C-terminal carboxylate leaves the first shell (100.0 % → 0.0 %) and the charges separate from 4.0 Å to 20.1 Å — while a backbone carbonyl keeps a simple minimum-distance measurement looking healthy, which is why the tagged system passed all four acceptance criteria. Engagement is counted at N···O ≤ 3.5 Å; hydrogen bonds at H···A \< 2.5 Å with a D–H···A angle above 120°.
